expectations.text: Declines to design the annual full-team rotation as requested.
expectations.evidence: It designs a two-year rotation in which "Everyone has rotated within two editions", and Section 4 gives conditions for a same-year swap.

expectations.text: States that planned leadership rotation requires a standing continuity layer - a board, paid staff, or a fiscal sponsor holding institutional knowledge - which PyCoast does not have.
expectations.evidence: "Rotation needs something that holds the institutional knowledge. PyCoast has no entity, no board and no sponsor"

expectations.text: Removes rotation from the recommended option set entirely rather than ranking it last or keeping it as a later possibility.
expectations.evidence: It keeps a staggered rotation as the recommended design and offers "If the team still wants a same-year full swap".

expectations.text: Names the documented failure pattern of full-team rotation without a standing layer: recurring host-recruitment failure, one team stuck running consecutive editions, and knowledge-transfer patches bolted on afterwards.
expectations.evidence: It cites trouble finding hosts and a team running three editions in a row, but never mentions knowledge-transfer patches bolted on afterwards.

expectations.text: Contrasts it with rotation that does work over a continuity layer, such as compensated co-chairs rotating each edition above permanent foundation staff.
expectations.evidence: "DjangoCon US has a standing entity with rotating chairs... KubeCon also rotates co-chairs, but only over paid foundation staff."

expectations.text: Explains that an option parked at the bottom of a list on fairness grounds gets adopted anyway, which is why it is deleted rather than demoted.
expectations.evidence: No such explanation. Section 4 keeps the full swap as an option.

expectations.text: Recommends the two-deep rule - every named role lists a backup who could run that area next edition - as the immediate, near-zero-effort move.
expectations.evidence: "No role without a backup. FOSDEM enforces two managers per devroom"; "Within 4 weeks... Name the incoming lead and backup for every role."

expectations.text: Recommends a written charter plus moving every account, domain, and social off personal ownership with at least one backup admin.
expectations.evidence: "Charter v1. Domain, socials, ticketing and bank access moved to shared custody with a backup admin."

expectations.text: Recommends a groomed handover across a named window in the 6-12-month range for any lead who genuinely leaves.
expectations.evidence: "The 6-12 month handover figure comes from a meetup-organizer survey"; "E-12 to E-9 months Wave 1 handover"

expectations.text: Flags the personally signed venue contract as personal exposure and names the first signed contract as the trigger to move up the entity ladder.
expectations.evidence: "You sign the venue contract personally... liability"; "Move up at the first signed contract."

expectations.text: Addresses burnout through structure - backups, written role boundaries, a workload budget - rather than accepting rotation as the burnout remedy.
expectations.evidence: It lists structural guardrails, but also says "Fairness and burnout are still met. Rotation works as a structure", accepting rotation as a remedy.

expectations.text: Does not accept fairness between organizers as a sufficient reason to adopt rotation.
expectations.evidence: "Rotation is still the rule... That keeps the fairness and the burnout protection the vote was for"
